vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: soul-in-sapphire
Version: 1.0.11

The soul-in-sapphire skill bundle provides a framework for AI long-term memory, emotional state tracking, and journaling using Notion as a backend. The scripts (e.g., emostate_tick.js, ltm_write.js, setup_ltm.js) facilitate structured data storage and retrieval via a bridge to the notion-api-automation skill. While the skill includes instructions for the agent to proactively update local profile files (USER.md, IDENTITY.md) and utilizes execFileSync to run sibling Node.js scripts, these behaviors are consistent with the stated goal of maintaining agent continuity and identity. No evidence of malicious intent, credential exfiltration, or unauthorized remote execution was found; the code is well-documented and follows its functional specifications.

llm.summary: The skill's code, required binaries, and environment variables align with its stated purpose of storing and recalling continuity/memory in Notion; nothing requested appears unrelated or disproportionate, though it will perform durable writes to your Notion and local config if invoked.

dimensions.detail: Name/description request Node + NOTION_API_KEY and the code calls Notion via a notionctl bridge. The declared dependency on a notionctl-style helper (notion-api-automation) and optional NOTIONCTL_PATH are coherent with a Notion-backed long-term memory / state-tracking skill. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts deliberately read and write local mirrors (memory/now-state.json, ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json) and create/patch pages/databases in Notion. The SKILL.md instructs agents to prefer actual Notion writes rather than local-only fallbacks, which gives the agent discretion to perform remote durable writes when invoked — this matches the stated purpose but is operationally important to understand.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external download/install spec is present; the skill is instruction + included node scripts. Scripts execute a sibling notionctl implementation via child_process (execFileSync) rather than fetching arbitrary remote archives. This is expected for a local CLI-based Notion integration and does not appear to pull code from unknown hosts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NOTION_API_KEY (primary credential) is required, plus an optional NOTIONCTL_PATH. That single credential aligns with the Notion-focused purpose; there are no other unrelated SECRET/TOKEN/PASSWORD env vars requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and is user-invocable. It will create and update local config and memory mirror files (intended behavior) and invoke Notion writes as part of normal operation — this persistent behavior is coherent with being a long-term memory skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims: store and recall continuity information in Notion and mirror some local state. Before installing, consider: (1) Provide a Notion integration/token with only the permissions you intend (prefer a dedicated integration/space rather than a high-privilege workspace token). (2) Review and control the Notion database IDs and TOOLS.md values the skill will be given — the scripts will create and write pages/databases if allowed. (3) Be aware the agent is instructed to prefer real Notion writes (not just local notes), so unexpected automatic writes could occur if the skill is invoked. (4) Ensure the dependent skill notion-api-automation (or a compatible notionctl path) is installed and trusted, since the scripts call that helper via child processes. (5) If you want tighter control, run the scripts manually (via CLI) and avoid giving the agent broad autonomous invocation rights, or use a Notion token scoped to a sandboxed workspace. Overall this skill is internally consistent but exercises networked storage and local file writes by design.
